why: A city at night from above; a phone screen lights with a map and a blue dot pulses into place.
Pull back from the phone up through the night sky to Earth in the dark field; the phone a single glowing point.
Satellites fade in on their orbits around Earth; three small clock marks light one by one as each verb lands.
One satellite traced around its orbit; a beam of light streaks across the field beside it.
The constellation fills in: orbital rings tilt around Earth, satellites travelling along them; the altitude marked on one radius line.
Close on one satellite; a clock face on its body ticks; rings of signal pulse outward from it and from the others.
One pulse carries two tags riding the wavefront: a position marker and a time stamp, each appearing on its words.
Signals arrive at the phone on the ground; an arrow from the phone upward is drawn and fades out, nothing leaves it.
One satellite fires a single pulse with its time stamp; the pulse travels down toward the phone.
The pulse in flight, the speed label riding beside it.
A timer on the phone counts while the pulse completes its trip, stopping as it arrives.
The two times sit on the phone; the arrival minus the sending gives travel time, which multiplies into a distance, each step on its word.
A straight line from satellite to phone, labelled; a direction arrow is offered and struck out.
The distance line sweeps around the satellite, drawing a full sphere (a circle in the flat picture) that grazes the Earth where the phone is.
A second satellite's sphere grows; where it crosses the first, a ring of overlap lights up.
A third sphere grows and the ring collapses to two bright points.

choice.delivery: a beat of hesitation on 'in principle'

why: One point drifts into the void and dims; the other sits on Earth's surface over the city and glows.
The glowing point flickers; the frame cuts in to the phone and its clock.
Two clocks side by side: the satellite's steady, the phone's visibly off its hand position.
A tiny tick of the clock unrolls into a long ruler across the city map, 300 metres long.
Back on the diagram: all three circles grow by the same amount and the single point breaks into a blurred patch with no common meeting.
The broken diagram holds still; the question appears beside it and the frame waits.
A fourth satellite rises over the horizon and its circle grows into the diagram.
Four unknown tiles light as named; then all four circles shrink together by the same amount until they snap to one shared point, and the phone's clock hand jumps to the right time.
Pull back up from the phone to a satellite in orbit; its clock comes into focus.
Two clocks side by side, ground and orbit; as the satellite speeds along its orbit, its clock falls behind.
The gravity well of Earth drawn shallowing with height; the orbit clock now races ahead of the ground clock.
The two effects as opposing pushes on the clock, the larger winning; the net gain settles on the orbit clock.
Back on the city map: a day counter runs and the blue dot slides steadily away from the phone across the city.
The satellite's clock is adjusted on the ground, launched, and in orbit its hands fall into step with the ground clock; the blue dot slides back home.
The diagram returns and replays in brief: pulse, timer, circles meeting, fourth circle snapping them to one point, each on its words.
The ground and orbit clocks tick together in step beside the replayed diagram.
Descend to the city: a signal bends slightly through the air and another reflects off a tall building; the blue dot shows a soft halo of uncertainty.
Back to the phone screen from the opening: the blue dot settles on the map; pull back to the night city and the satellites passing above.

check fails only on kit tight_inset: scenes/_kit.js signal mkChip (~lines 647-659) pill w = 56+tw leaves its text box flush (-0.5px) with the pill edge; needs pill w = 56+tw+16. Affects b07 (and any beat using signal pinText/stampText).

Root cause of b07 tight_inset on part signal found: the probe's containerOf (runtime/kit.js 388-412) skips offset shadows only when they carry class "lm-shadow". The chip's shadow rect (scenes/_kit.js line 651, mkChip) has no class, so the probe takes it as the pill: it sits 8px lower (y -20..36), the 41px-high text (y -20.5..20.5) is 0.5px above its top edge, inset -0.5. The earlier width fix (w = 56+tw+16) could not matter: the limiting side is the top. Fix: add class: "lm-shadow" to that shadow rect attributes. Nothing else changes.
